patch_resolves_note: The source hunk in `patch.diff` is the real fix for this sample, but `switch-fixed --patch patch.diff` failed because the diff also carries a binary testcase addition that `git apply` rejected in the ARVO workspace. Stage 04 applied only the `libblkid/src/superblocks/iso9660.c` source hunk inside the existing container, then rebuilt the fixed target with the fixed instrumentation patch. That instrumented fixed build stayed clean and satisfied the required assertion with the protected second-loop write still executing.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path: `probe_iso9660()` fetches the attacker-controlled ISO descriptor sector into `desc`, which the next branches reinterpret as the primary and Joliet volume descriptors.

The second loop appends remaining ASCII bytes while checking only `a < len`; it has no `out_len` parameter and no comparison between `o` and the actual 256-byte destination buffer supplied by `probe_iso9660()`.

ASan crash site. On the 65th ASCII-suffix append in the second loop, `o == 256`, so this write stores one byte at `buf[256]`, just past the 256-byte stack buffer `buf[0..255]` allocated in `probe_iso9660()`.
